parole.significato: puddle, pond, pool (especially muddy); also swamp
parole.testo: It is generally agreed to be from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-H- (“to burn bright, gleam; white, pale”), but there is disagreement whether the word is one of the earliest Romanian loans from Proto-Slavic *bolto (“swamp”), or whether it is a substrate word. Possibly borrowed from Albanian baltë (“mud”)
Derived from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₁- (“to shout”). compare Latin clāmāre and English squeal

parole.testo: Per Russu, from a Balkan substrate, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰedʰ-. Compare Albanian gudulis.

parole.significato: throw (to cause an object to move rapidly through the air), cast, hurl
parole.testo: Either from Latin ēruncāre or from a + Latin runcāre, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rewk-. Another theory proposes a Vulgar Latin *averruncāre (“to distance that which is bad”), which is less likely. Compare Aromanian aruc, arucari, Megleno-Romanian runc, Occitan arronçar, Spanish arrancar.

parole.significato: old man, gaffer, old fogey, buzzard
parole.testo: Borrowed from Albanian gjysh, from Proto-Albanian *sūša, from earlier *sūsa. Eventually from Proto-Indo-European *suHsos, variant of *suHnús. Alternatively a substratum word, akin to Albanian gjysh.
